newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Colruyt splitting, not selling Dolmen.
newsitem.headline: Colruyt splitting, not selling Dolmen.

text.p: Belgian retailer Colruyt on Thursday denied stock market rumours it was about to sell Dolmen Computer Applications, but said it would split it into two on July 1 and might sell one of the units at a later stage.
"The external part will be split from the internal part from July 1," chief executive officer Rene De Wit told Reuters.
He said the external part -- which provides software services to clients other than Colruyt and also sells hardware and network installations -- could now be sold off if needed.
"There are no plans for the moment, but if there would ever be an opportunity, we can respond to it," De Wit said.
"If it is to the benefit of the company, if it would ever be necessary for Dolmen External to have a major expansion, if ever Colruyt has to yield 100 percent, we can now do so," he said.

Colruyt had been preparing the split for about half a year. "Suppose somebody now says 'I want to take a stake in Dolmen' ...we decided to make it possible without touching Dolmen Internal, on which our distribution activity depends too much," he said.
Dolmen's Internal mainly represents Colruyt data processing -- the computer division of the Colruyt group.
De Wit said turnover of the exteral part was much bigger than that of the internal part mainly due to sales of hardware.
Workforce of the external part was about 400, of the internal division 250.
The Dolmen rumours were cited as one of the main reasons behind Colruyt's 8.2 percent leap on the Brussels bourse on Thursday.
